_about: WORLD [every job kind], 10/24/26, rule 153(b) (Paolo 10/24: 'right now the only jobs you have are pull up on people and kill them, but in Battle Brothers there were a lot of different jobs: find something on the map, or do a caravan, or roam around until you find a certain enemy type and kill a bunch of them; I want more quest types'). Every board job is ONE KIND from QUESTS' table (questbook/research/QR_AF_THE_CONTRACT_KINDS_10_9_26.md, research only, read never asked), and the kind decides how it plays on the map: slices/bohemia_job_kinds.js reads this file and the map's one job loop (__THE_LOOP_ON_THE_MAP__ in slices/BOHEMIA_CITY_WORLD.html) hands every held job to it. A MODDER EDITS THIS FILE: give an offer id a kind under 'offers', or add a line to 'guess' (a title pattern) and every new board row gets it; a kind's numbers are shapes, TUNING owns their values. draft:true.
source: questbook/research/QR_AF_THE_CONTRACT_KINDS_10_9_26.md (THE TABLE and THE ROWS); Battle Brothers' numbers quoted there from the wiki dump

beasts_by_ground._why: BEASTS 2 11/3 (rule 345 amended (b), Paolo 11/3: 'everything's looking like a fucking coyote'; ask line 381): a job whose foe is 'beasts' meets the beasts of the ground its fight is on, by weight; a canid is one choice among many, never the default. The ground is WORLD's (records/target/BOHEMIA_BOARD_KINDS.json districts); the habitats are the animals' own (records/target/bb/bohemia_enemies.json rows: the coyote the suburbs' edges and the parks, the hog the water, the camel and the bull the open desert, the lion the hills). A job that names its animal (foe 'wolves', 'dogs', 'lions' ...) meets that animal. draft: TUNING owns the weights. WORLD 9 11/5 (rules 389 and 399(c), __THE_GIANTS_ARE_RARE__): the slow lab giants (giants.kinds: the sabre-tooth, the short-faced bear, the ground sloth, the American lion, Camelops) are out of every ground's mix, so no pack, hunt or guard is ever one; each is a named rare hunt of its own (big game). The hills and the open desert are the real Mojave's in their place: wild burros and horses (Red Rock's burros), coyotes, a mountain lion now and then (a lion hunts alone: beast_looks pack_max).

foe_says._why: JOBS 11/10 (rule 443(c); EYES row 551): who they were, handed to the end screen by every job's fight (slices/bohemia_job_kinds.js __EVERY_JOB_NAMES_ITS_FOE__), keyed by the fight's part of the job; a row's own foe_says first; a beast is always named as itself (beast_looks label). {what} the job's thing, {cargo}, {item}, {place}, {from} the client's town, {dest} the town it goes to, {label} the fight's own words. draft:true: WORDS' to overwrite
foe_says.band: the crew on the patrol road
foe_says.gate: the crew at the gate of {dest}
foe_says.ambush: the ones who lay in wait

beast_looks._why: BEASTS 2 11/3: the map draws each beast party from that animal's own fight sheet (slices/fight_rig/fight_rig.json looks, sizes read from the index the fight reads), and the job's words name it. WORLD 9 11/5: pack_max is the most of that animal that stand together (a mountain lion hunts alone or with one more; a giant is always one).

giants._why: WORLD 9 11/5 (rule 389's default, rule 399(c); Paolo 11/4: 'the amount of beasts I'm slaying, I feel like that's not realistic... I keep going all around the city just killing the sabre-tooth tigers'). The slow lab giants: a clone farm makes tens a year and these cannot breed back (Dolly had six lambs; a sabre-tooth's surrogate is a lion with one cub a year), so they are never a pack, never a hunt's quarry, never a job's guard; each is ONE animal, a named rare hunt on a board (big game, its own row's legs), so a hunt for one is an event. The fast lab lines (dire wolves, bison, hogs) and the ferals the dead feed (dogs, coyotes, cattle, burros) are the packs. max_share is the gate's line: across a seeded month of boards, giant fights at most this share of all the jobs' fights. BESTIARY 11/9 (rule 440(f)): the American cheetah, the Ice Age jaguar and the long-horned bison are slow giants too (a big cat or a giant bison, one young a year, never bred back); the goats, the stilt-legged horses, the llamas and the shrub-oxen are herds.

clear-crew.plays: the crew is marked a few blocks out; reach it, the fight, paid there. Today's job, unchanged.

haul-caravan.plays: the cargo is a truck that follows you to another town; it is slow (every block costs the clock more); you still tap where to go and where to stop; raiders come for it on the road; each crate that arrives pays its share; a lost fight loses half of what is left; nothing left and the job is lost
haul-caravan.pace_why: Battle Brothers: you lose control and walk at the caravan's speed; ours keeps the controls and keeps the slowness as the clock (QR-AF H1 DIFFERENT)
haul-caravan.ambush_why: Battle Brothers' escort meets one or two parties on the road; a three-star caravan is the one worth two
haul-caravan.ambush_extra_why: raiders who come for a cargo come with one more than a party on the road
haul-caravan.lost_fight_why: the wiki: losing some cargo halves the pay; ours, per crate, so a lost fight takes half of what is left
haul-caravan.fallen_why: a man of yours who went down dropped the crate he was guarding
haul-caravan.twist_why: QR-AF: one escort in five; T18 a third party says the cargo is stolen (one more fight at the gate), T13 your own crew eyes the cargo (a crate walks off in the night)

find-place.plays: the client says which way and how far; the map rings where to look; walk inside the ring and it turns up within two blocks; go back to the client to be paid (Battle Brothers pays on the return)
find-place.twist_why: QR-AF F1: the 20% the directions lead into an ambush, a fight where you find it

find-person.plays: a FIND, and the ones you found walk home with you like a caravan's cargo, a head for a crate; paid at the client's town for every head that comes home
find-person.twist_why: QR-AF F3: one in four, the found do not all want to come; one stays

hunt-kind.plays: packs of the named kind roam the ground around the town; meet them (tap a pack and you go after it, contact is the fight), kill until the count on the job reaches what the client asked, then go back to the client to be paid; packs that are gone are replaced, farther out
hunt-kind.twist_why: QR-AF B2: the rarest, one hunt in ten, the last of them a mother with young

clear-camp.plays: a camp stands on the map, bigger than a party (a fire, its men); reach it, the fight; paid there, part flat and part a head for every one put down, capped at the camp's size
clear-camp.twist_why: QR-AF K2: one in four, the client lied: half of them are families, not fighters; fewer stand up, the pay is the same

carry.plays: one thing in the bag to another town, no truck and no slowness; paid when it is signed for there; thieves may wait on the road, and if they win it goes to their lair, a camp off the road, to be taken back
carry.twist_why: QR-AF C1: one delivery in five; the wiki's 'brigands steal it and leave tracks to their lair', which turns it into a CLEAR

hold-defend.plays: the client's gate is marked HOLD with the nights left; stand on it before then and they come, wave after wave, one fight each; every wave held pays its share, all held pays the job; not there in time and the place is raided
hold-defend.waves_why: Battle Brothers: up to three parties attack
hold-defend.days_why: QR-AF rule: a clock only on HOLD; the client's words say the nights
hold-defend.twist_why: QR-AF D1's 20% kidnapping (T10) needs the chase this lane has not built; the HOLD's own clock is its hardness

recover-return.plays: the thing is somewhere in the valley with whoever has it now (men, beasts, or nobody); reach it, the fight where somebody holds it, take it, bring it back to the client to be paid; a lost fight leaves it there and the job open

guess.why: there and back on a route: a patrol, before the escort's 'walk'
the client's own verb: a thing or people walked to another place

place_why: WORLD [the PC playtest: the jobs' part] (1), rule 164 item 3, Paolo 10/24 on his PC: 'take three carts to Prim, and it's really just the blue settlement.' A row's 'place' is the place its words name. {name, real}: one of the region's real places (engine/BOHEMIA_REGION_LAND.json places, by name) or a valley town (ctBases, by name), and the job goes THERE (the carts to PRIMM, the relief shift and the intake deck to HOOVER DAM, the letter over RAILROAD PASS, the pharmacy at MT CHARLESTON LODGE, the freezer at the fossil beds, TULE SPRINGS); {name}: a place the words make up ('the pump station'), a block the dice pick, carrying that name on the map; 'way': the words' own direction ('the south road'). No place: the words name none ('the pack that drinks here'), and the job's place is the client's own town. The map names every place a held job names and rings the next one; off the glass, its name waits at the glass's edge, pointing. Names are draft:true.
default_why: a job no row names and no pattern matches is today's job, a crew marked on the map, so a new board row is never broken by this file

pay_marks.why: WORLD 4 (rule 308, ask line 301; Paolo 11/2: 'the job has to be quickly identifiable as do I need to return back to the job site or I can just handle it out there... maybe it's like a different color'): the mark first on every line a job shows on. Amber with a return arrow for come back, green with a pin for paid there, both the phone's own colours; never purple (the Amalgamation's). His to change.

timing.hunt_spread_why: WORLD 4 [a job's time is the truth] (rule 307, Paolo 11/2): a hunt is the one job that cannot be exact, because the packs move (they wander every other block and come at him from four blocks off), so its time is said as a range around the walk to the nearest packs until the count is met and home: the low end a quarter short (they came to him), the high end three tenths long (they wandered off). Set from the probe's hunts (tools/bohemia_world_job_time_probe.js); his to change.

board_people._about: WORLD [every job kind]: board people this file adds to the shelf (slices/bohemia_board_shelf.js appends them when both load), for a kind none of QUESTS' 96 act-one designs carries. Shaped exactly like the shelf's rows: two sentences, the pay in the second as {pay}. Names and words are attempts, draft:true; QUESTS or RUN TWO may replace them with a design.

rows.title: Walk the two pump posts and back

client.name: Ingeniero Robles
client.from: who keeps the turbines

rows.says: Two pump posts on the dam road went quiet this week, and quiet out there means somebody is listening. Walk to both and back, and it pays {pay} batteries at most, part of it for every crew you stop on the way.

rows.title: Ride the wash line and back

client.name: Doña Inés
client.from: who counts the water

rows.says: Somebody cuts our hose along the wash at night, never the same place twice. Ride out to the two posts and back, and {pay} batteries are yours at most, more of it if you catch them at it.

rows.title: Hit the convoy at the cut

client.name: Ramiro Salas
client.from: who buys what the trucks carry

rows.says: A convoy comes down the dry road tonight with batteries that should be ours. Wait for it at the cut and stop it, and it pays {pay} batteries.

rows.title: Walk the water clerk to the next town

client.name: Licenciada Mora
client.from: who keeps the water ledger

rows.says: Our clerk has to carry the ledger to the next town, and men want that ledger. Walk him there safe and he pays you {pay} batteries at their gate.

rows.title: Bring in the man they call Chuy Lento

client.name: Comandante Rivas
client.from: who keeps the peace here, badly

rows.says: Chuy Lento took two of our girls' carts and only comes out after dark. Bring me his red ring and it pays {pay} batteries.

rows.title: Look at the three wells and come tell me

client.name: Tía Nena
client.from: who waters the whole block

rows.says: Three wells out there, and I don't know which still give water or who is sitting on them. Go look at all three and tell me, and it pays {pay} batteries.

rows.title: Burn the tire yard down

client.name: El Profe
client.from: who teaches kids in a bus

rows.says: The tire yard sells to whoever pays, and whoever pays is shooting at us. Burn it to the ground and it pays {pay} batteries.

rows.title: Collect what Don Beto owes

client.name: Doña Chela
client.from: who lends batteries at the corner

rows.says: Don Beto owes me forty and smiles at me in the street like we're friends. Bring it back, however you do it, and {pay} batteries are yours.

rows.title: Kill the old lion of the golf course
rows.rare_why: WORLD 9 11/5 (rules 389, 399(c)): a slow giant is a named rare hunt, up on a place's board one window in five (bohemia_job_danger.js rareUp)

client.name: Señor Whitlock
client.from: who used to own the golf course

rows.says: The lab lion sleeps on my old eighteenth hole and eats my goats. One beast, very big. Kill it and it pays {pay} batteries.

rows.title: Find where the three a.m. voice comes from

client.name: Nacho Radio
client.from: who fixes radios for food

rows.says: Every night at three a woman's voice comes on every radio in the camp, reading prices. Find what is making it, and it pays {pay} batteries.

rows.title: Get our people out of the pen

client.name: Padre Tomás
client.from: who counts the missing

rows.says: They keep our people in a dog pen and sell them to the mines. Open that pen and bring one of them home to me, and it pays {pay} batteries.

rows.title: Clear the den in the old water park

client.name: Gordo Ruiz
client.from: who keeps the goats on Lake Mead Boulevard

rows.says: Something sleeps in the old water park and takes a goat every night. Find where it sleeps and clear it out, and it pays {pay} batteries.

rows.title: Find out what is in the stew

client.name: Doña Chelo
client.from: whose grandson eats at the stew cart

rows.says: My grandson eats at the stew cart every night and comes home happy. Find out what is in that stew for me, and it pays {pay} batteries.

rows.title: Find what the vultures found

client.name: Rafa Quintero
client.from: who runs the camp kitchen

rows.says: The vultures have circled past the wash since morning, so something big is dead out there. Go see what it is and tell me where, and it pays {pay} batteries and a share.

rows.title: Follow the man who brings the drug

client.name: Sor Inés
client.from: who runs the clinic and counts the overdoses

rows.says: Every Thursday a man walks the drug down Boulder Highway and the clinic fills up. Follow him and tell me who he answers to, and it pays {pay} batteries.

rows.title: Hold the grow house when the power is out

client.name: Sal Benedetti
client.from: who runs the Mob's farms

rows.says: The power to the grow house is out and every crew in the valley knows it. Sit on it with my people until the lights come back, and the Family pays {pay} batteries.

rows.title: Kill the sabre-tooth in the red rocks
rows.rare_why: WORLD 9 11/5 (rules 389, 399(c)): a slow giant is a named rare hunt, up on a place's board one window in five (bohemia_job_danger.js rareUp)

client.name: Dr. Halvorsen
client.from: who used to feed it at the lab

rows.says: One of my sabre-tooths has lived in the red rocks since the fences went down, and it is very good at killing. Bring me proof it is dead and it pays {pay} batteries.

rows.title: Bring down the sloth at Tule Springs
rows.rare_why: WORLD 9 11/5 (rules 389, 399(c)): a slow giant is a named rare hunt, up on a place's board one window in five (bohemia_job_danger.js rareUp)

client.name: Professor Dade
client.from: who dug the fossil beds before the crash

rows.says: The lab grew one ground sloth and it walked home to Tule Springs, where its bones were found, and now it flattens tents. Put it down and it pays {pay} batteries.

rows.title: Walk the propane tanks to the truck stop

client.name: Lalo Ferrán
client.from: who fills the tanks behind the laundromat

rows.says: Six tanks on a cart and a road with nobody on it, which is what worries me. Walk them to the truck stop, and every tank that gets there is part of {pay} batteries.

rows.title: Bring the seed sacks up from the river

client.name: Hermana Rocío
client.from: who keeps the greenhouse alive

rows.says: The seed came up the river from Laughlin and somebody already knows it did. Bring the sacks to us whole, and {pay} batteries, less for every sack you lose.

rows.title: Ride with the clinic's van to the hospital

client.name: Doctora Amaya
client.from: who runs the clinic out of a school

rows.says: The van carries every pill we have left and three crews want it. Ride with it to the hospital and keep it moving, and it pays {pay} batteries if the boxes get there.

rows.title: Hold the pump house till morning

client.name: Don Abel
client.from: who keeps the water running

rows.says: They came for the pump house last week and broke the lock. They will come again before the week is out. Stand there when they do, and {pay} batteries.

rows.title: Keep the market standing two nights

client.name: Señora Quintero
client.from: who rents the stalls

rows.says: Twice they kicked the stalls over and took the till. Keep the market standing two nights, and it pays {pay} batteries.

rows.title: Hold the substation three nights

client.name: Ingeniera Paz
client.from: who keeps the last lines live

rows.says: The substation is the only light this side of the wash. They know it, and they keep coming. Hold it three nights, and {pay} batteries.

rows.title: Carry the cold box to the camp

client.name: Enfermera Lupe
client.from: who sleeps next to the fridge

rows.says: A cold box of insulin, and a girl at the camp who needs it by Friday. Carry it there and get it signed for, and {pay} batteries.

rows.title: Carry the deed to the courthouse

client.name: Licenciado Barrera
client.from: who still files papers nobody reads

rows.says: A deed, a stamp and a man at the courthouse who will make it real. Some people would rather it never got there. Carry it, and {pay} batteries.

rows.title: Carry the fuses over the pass

client.name: Maestro Tirado
client.from: who fixes what the grid broke

rows.says: Twelve fuses, the last ones in the valley, and the other side of the pass is dark without them. Carry them over, and {pay} batteries when they are signed for.

rows.title: Run the squatters off the car lot

client.name: Chuy Valdés
client.from: who wants his lot back

rows.says: A crew moved onto my car lot and strips the cars at night. Run them off, and {pay} batteries, and more for every one you put down.

rows.title: Clear the crew out of the motel

client.name: Madre Inés
client.from: who runs the soup line

rows.says: The motel by the freeway was ours, beds for the soup line. A crew took it and charges at the door. Clear them out, and {pay} batteries.

rows.title: Take back the bus yard

client.name: Comandante Ruelas
client.from: who wants the buses running

rows.says: Forty buses and the diesel to move them, and a gang sitting on all of it. Take the yard back, and it pays {pay} batteries.

rows.title: Collect what Tito owes the bar

client.name: Mama Ceci
client.from: who runs the bar with no sign

rows.says: Tito drank a month on my tab and moved across the wash. Bring back what he owes, however you do it, and {pay} batteries.

rows.title: Collect the rent from the garage

client.name: Don Ignacio
client.from: who owns the street, on paper

rows.says: The garage on my street has not paid in three months and keeps the lights on with my power. Collect the rent, and {pay} batteries.

rows.title: Collect the casino's markers

client.name: El Gordo Baez
client.from: who still keeps the casino's books

rows.says: A man owes the house markers from before the money died, and the house never forgets. Collect them, and {pay} batteries.

rows.title: Root out the Cartel's stash houses

client.name: Sargento Dolores Quintero
client.from: who runs the Remnants' night watch

rows.says: The Cartel keeps two stash houses past the wash, and every gun in them ends up pointed at us. Put both out of business, and {pay} batteries.

rows.title: Close the two houses the Pures keep

client.name: Hermana Luz Ocampo
client.from: who runs the Church's soup line

rows.says: The Pures keep two houses on our side of the wash, and they recruit out of my soup line. Close both houses, mijo, and {pay} batteries.

rows.title: Root out the skim rooms off the Strip

client.name: Tony Calabrese
client.from: who counts for the Mob on the Strip

rows.says: Somebody runs two skim rooms off my tables. I want them gone, both, the same night. {pay} batteries, and the Strip remembers your face.

rows.title: Break the ring round the truck stop

client.name: Mamá Ruth Okafor
client.from: who runs the Caravans' yard

rows.says: The Cartel has us ringed: a crew on each road in, and their tow trucks parked at the edge so nothing leaves. Break all three, and {pay} batteries.

rows.title: Break the ring round the co-op's gardens

client.name: Wren Halvorsen
client.from: who keeps the co-op's water

rows.says: Three crews are sitting on the roads round our gardens, waiting for us to starve. We voted on it: {pay} batteries to move them.

rows.title: Break the ring round the solar yard

client.name: Ignacio “Nacho” Villaseñor
client.from: who keeps the Trades' panels

rows.says: Two crews and a dozer have the solar yard boxed in. The Trades do not take sides, so I am not asking you to. Just open the roads. {pay} batteries.

rows.title: Get the drive out of the dead data center

client.name: Celeste Varga
client.from: who speaks for the Network

rows.says: There is a drive in the old data center, and the people sleeping there do not know what it is. Bring it to me, and {pay} batteries. Do not plug it in.

rows.title: Get the press die out of the old can plant

client.name: Abuela Rosario Tafoya
client.from: who runs the Trades' machine shop

rows.says: The die for the can press is still in the old plant. No die, no cans, and no cans means nobody keeps food. Bring it back, {pay} batteries.

rows.title: Get the club's film reels back

client.name: Mari Duarte
client.from: who runs the Colorful's club

rows.says: Our old club burned, but the film reels in the basement did not. Fifty years of us, on film. Bring them home, and {pay} batteries.

rows.title: Make the old school safe again

client.name: Ms. Adaeze Nwosu
client.from: who teaches for the Volunteers

rows.says: The old school on the east side has people squatting in it. Clear it, come back for my teachers, and walk them there. {pay} batteries when the kids can sit down.

rows.title: Give the chapel by the overpass back

client.name: Padre Teodoro Alcalá
client.from: who keeps the Church's books

rows.says: The chapel by the overpass was ours before the crash. Clear out who took it, then walk my people back in. {pay} batteries, and a prayer if you want one.

rows.title: Open the tunnel pump room again

client.name: Old Man Cassius
client.from: who speaks for the King Hobo

rows.says: The pump room keeps the tunnels dry, and something moved into it. Clear it, then walk my fixers down. {pay} batteries, and the tunnels are open to you.

rows.title: Find the singer who walked off

client.name: Rook
client.from: who books the Anarchists' shows

rows.says: Our singer walked out after the last show and never came back. Find her. {pay} batteries, and you are on the guest list for life.

rows.title: Find the clerk who ran with the ledgers

client.name: Whitfield Ames
client.from: who keeps the Reds' accounts

rows.says: A clerk ran with our ledgers. Find him and bring him back, ledgers and all. {pay} batteries, and the Reds owe you one.

rows.title: Find the three dealers who skipped town

client.name: Nina Moretti
client.from: who runs the Mob's card rooms

rows.says: Three of my dealers skipped town owing the house. Bring all three back, breathing. {pay} batteries.

rows.title: Walk the water drums to the dry camp

client.name: Teo Abernathy
client.from: who drives the Caravans' water truck

rows.says: Four drums of water for the dry camp, and the road there has teeth. Walk them in, and every drum that arrives is part of {pay} batteries.

rows.title: Walk the costume trunks to the old bandshell

client.name: Dulce Paredes
client.from: who dresses the Colorful's shows

rows.says: Three trunks of costumes, forty years of sequins. The show at the bandshell is in two nights. Get them there, {pay} batteries.

rows.title: Walk the strongbox to the tower bank

client.name: Margaret Kell
client.from: who signs for the Reds' vault

rows.says: One strongbox, and half the valley knows what is in it. Walk it to the tower bank with your crew around it. {pay} batteries.

rows.title: Watch the clinic tent through the night

client.name: Dr. Imani Okoye
client.from: who runs the Volunteers' clinic tent

rows.says: Somebody wants our medicine, and they come at night. Stand by the tent till morning. {pay} batteries, and one of my nurses goes home with you.

rows.title: Keep the tunnel mouth through the night

client.name: Little Abe
client.from: who keeps the King Hobo's doors

rows.says: Something comes up out of the old flood tunnel after dark and takes what it wants. Sit on the tunnel mouth till sunup. {pay} batteries.

rows.title: Hold the fuel depot until dawn

client.name: Teniente Marco Ybarra
client.from: who keeps the Remnants' fuel

rows.says: The Cartel hits the fuel depot every night we leave it. Not tonight. Hold it until dawn, and {pay} batteries.

rows.title: Carry the speakers to the show

client.name: Jinx Calloway
client.from: who runs the Anarchists' sound

rows.says: We got speakers for the show, a whole stack, do not ask from where. Carry them over to the stage, {pay} batteries.

rows.title: Bring the panels down off the old school roof

client.name: Benito Saldaña
client.from: who buys for the Trades' yard

rows.says: The old school roof has six good panels nobody is using. Bring them down to the yard, {pay} batteries. Nobody will miss them.

rows.title: Walk the courier to the old relay

client.name: Celeste Varga
client.from: who speaks for the Network

rows.says: A courier of ours needs to reach the old relay tower with what he carries. Walk him there, and do not let him talk to anyone. {pay} batteries.

rows.title: Clear the water plant for the co-op

client.name: Wren Halvorsen
client.from: who keeps the co-op's water

rows.says: The old water plant could water every garden we have. The Reds want it too. Clear it for us, {pay} batteries, and we owe you water.

rows.title: Clear the water plant for the Reds

client.name: Whitfield Ames
client.from: who keeps the Reds' accounts

rows.says: Whoever holds the water plant sets the price of water. We would like that to be us. Clear it, {pay} batteries.

rows.title: Clear the old TV station for the Network

client.name: Celeste Varga
client.from: who speaks for the Network

rows.says: The old TV station still has its mast. We want it. So do the Anarchists, for their pirate radio. Clear it for us, {pay} batteries.

rows.title: Clear the old TV station for the pirate radio

client.name: Rook
client.from: who books the Anarchists' shows

rows.says: Give us that mast and the whole valley hears the truth every night. The Network wants it too. Clear it for us. {pay} batteries.

rows.title: Clear the market hall for a shelter

client.name: Hermana Luz Ocampo
client.from: who runs the Church's soup line

rows.says: The big market hall could sleep three hundred people this winter. The Mob wants it for a card room. Clear it for us, mijo, {pay} batteries.

rows.title: Clear the market hall for a card room

client.name: Nina Moretti
client.from: who runs the Mob's card rooms

rows.says: The market hall is the best floor on the east side. The Church wants it for cots. Clear it for us, {pay} batteries.
